target.name: NetworkOcean
target.founder: Sam Mendel (CEO; serial founder, prior exit of a creator-hiring marketplace), Eric Kim (CTO; ex-Palantir, Merge; Cornell)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
NetworkOcean is a seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Sam Mendel (serial founder with a prior marketplace exit) and Eric Kim (ex-Palantir and Merge engineer). The company has raised $1M to date. The comparable universe consists of three private peers in the ocean and maritime sector—Standard Subsea, Clippership, and Albacore—with no public market comparables available.

The valuation analysis applies stage-progression methodology, which is the applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using $1M in total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $2M. This reflects the expected markup investors apply when moving from seed financing into Series A or equivalent follow-on rounds.

The analysis triangulates to a range of $2.125M (low) to $2.875M (high), with a median of $2.5M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than convergence across multiple approaches. The primary uncertainties stem from the absence of public comparables and limited data on private peer valuations, making it difficult to validate multiples or assess relative positioning within the ocean-tech sector. Meaningful refinement would require additional private transaction data or clarity on financial metrics (revenue, runway, product adoption).
